questions.question: What is currying in JavaScript? Implement a curry function.
questions.title: Currying in JavaScript — Implementation, Use Cases & Examples
questions.direct_answer:
What is currying in JavaScript? Implement a curry function.

**In one line:** name the mechanism, where it applies (the type checker, emit pipeline, and how types line up with runtime JS), and the user-visible outcome.

**Interviewers dig into:** Currying transforms f(a,b,c) into f(a)(b)(c); implementation via closures and arity checking; use cases in partial application and function composition.

**Classic weak answer:** Confusing currying (one arg at a time) with partial application (fixing some args); mismatched handling of variadic calls.

**Senior finish:** Show a generic curry that supports f(1,2)(3), f(1)(2,3), f(1)(2)(3); use cases in Redux selectors, event handlers, validation.

interviewer_intent.testing: Currying transforms f(a,b,c) into f(a)(b)(c); implementation via closures and arity checking; use cases in partial application and function composition
interviewer_intent.common_mistake: Confusing currying (one arg at a time) with partial application (fixing some args); mismatched handling of variadic calls
interviewer_intent.to_stand_out: Show a generic curry that supports f(1,2)(3), f(1)(2,3), f(1)(2)(3); use cases in Redux selectors, event handlers, validation

sections.title: Why this question matters
sections.content:
This question — **Currying in JavaScript — Implementation, Use Cases & Examples** — shows up constantly in **frontend / fullstack** interviews because it separates candidates who memorized docs from candidates who can **reason about real systems**.

**Restate the prompt:** What is currying in JavaScript? Implement a curry function.

A gold-level answer does four things in order:

1. **Define** the terms in plain English (what it is / what problem it solves).
2. **Explain the mechanism** (what runs when: browser, bundler, framework, network).
3. **Compare trade-offs** (speed vs correctness vs security vs DX) with **when you would not use** the default.
4. **Ground it in production** — caching, auth, observability, tests, or an incident you handled.

Interviewers are listening for: **Currying transforms f(a,b,c) into f(a)(b)(c); implementation via closures and arity checking; use cases in partial application and function composition**.

The fastest way to lose points is: **Confusing currying (one arg at a time) with partial application (fixing some args); mismatched handling of variadic calls**.

If you only add one “senior” layer, make it: **Show a generic curry that supports f(1,2)(3), f(1)(2,3), f(1)(2)(3); use cases in Redux selectors, event handlers, validation**.

sections.title: Deep dive — what to say
sections.content:
### What to explain (middle of the answer)

- **Core mechanics:** Currying transforms f(a,b,c) into f(a)(b)(c); implementation via closures and arity checking; use cases in partial application and function composition
- **Concrete shape:** give a small code or config snippet *only if it clarifies* (5–15 lines max).
- **Interviewer follow-ups:** expect “what breaks in production?”, “how do you debug?”, “what would you measure?” — answer them proactively.

### How to sound senior (without rambling)

- Tie the feature to **user-visible outcomes** (performance, accessibility, security).
- Mention **one failure mode** you have actually seen (race, stale cache, hydration mismatch, flaky test).
- Close with **one decision rule** (“choose X when …; choose Y when …”).

questions.question: What is the difference between function composition and partial application?
questions.title: Function Composition vs Partial Application — Differences Explained
questions.direct_answer:
What is the difference between function composition and partial application?

**In one line:** name the mechanism, where it applies (the type checker, emit pipeline, and how types line up with runtime JS), and the user-visible outcome.

**Interviewers dig into:** Composition chains functions (compose(f,g)(x) = f(g(x))); partial application fixes some args of a function; both use closures.

**Classic weak answer:** Using pipe vs compose in the wrong order — pipe is left-to-right; compose is right-to-left.

**Senior finish:** Implement pipe and compose in 3 lines each; mention Ramda and lodash/fp; link to React's HOCs as compose in the wild.
